findings.claim: The change has no regression test covering the fix: the only colocated test covers the useImportSafe hook, not the component's re-render behavior, so there is no SafeAccountInput component test verifying that the success icon appears after a valid Safe resolves. If someone later reverts useWatch back to watch(...), which looks like a harmless simplification, this regression would only be caught by Maestro e2e flows, if at all.

A SafeAccountInput.test.tsx should be added that renders the component inside a real FormProvider, mocks useLazySafeOverviews to resolve with data, and asserts that the success-icon test ID appears; it should also assert the width-20 placeholder view renders while isFetching is true or errors.safeAddress is set.

The newly added inline comment explaining the watch vs useWatch difference is not required by any cited convention, and the only other useWatch call in the mobile app (ImportAccountFormView.tsx:26) has no such comment, so the comment's presence is inconsistent with existing usage; it could instead be replaced by the recommended regression test, which would guard the behavior without relying on prose.
